title: Copilot Studio: app- and intent-first agent creation experience
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the planned creation experience from documented Copilot Studio behaviour. The credit-allocation API is supported despite the automated warning; minor corrections should clarify existing product licensing, complete the control path and request-property note, and reconcile checklist controls with the table.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no licence specific to this creation experience has been published.
claims.quote: To use Copilot Studio, you need one of the following configurations: ... Copilot Studio user license (free) ... Copilot Studio authors ... Microsoft 365 Copilot license ... Copilot Studio trial license.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the unpublished-licence wording with: 'This creation option sits inside Copilot Studio's existing access model. For standard-harness authoring, Learn lists a free Copilot Studio user license backed by a tenant prepaid Copilot Credit pack subscription, Copilot Studio authors access for applicable pay-as-you-go scenarios, a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, or a Copilot Studio trial license. No licence specific to the app-first flow is published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing. Keep the separate uncertainty about which harness this flow uses and its building charges.

claims.claim: Agents, workflows and apps powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness use Copilot Credits for usage-based billing.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the start of building, unlike the standard harness which starts billing after publish.

claims.claim: Administrators can allocate prepaid Copilot Credits to environments.
claims.quote: As a Power Platform administrator, you can use controls in the Power Platform admin center to allocate prepaid credits, limit consumption, monitor usage, and identify agents created through the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: Turning off Draw from the available capacity in my tenant contains prepaid consumption at the environment allocation.
claims.quote: To contain prepaid consumption, allocate a defined amount of Copilot Credits to the environment and turn off Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.claim: Usage can still continue through a linked pay-as-you-go billing plan when tenant-capacity draw is off.
claims.quote: If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: The allocation and tenant-capacity control is reached through Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Licensing. Under Products, select Copilot Studio, and then select Manage Copilot Credits. ... Select the environment ... Under Allocate capacity ... Under Capacity overages, select or clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant
claims.fix: The path stops on the correct control page. Extend it to 'Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment' and add to the note: 'Under Allocate capacity, enter the allocation; under Capacity overages, select or clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.' Use the same wording in the rendered table.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 sets environment allocations and tenant-capacity draw.
claims.quote: All programmatic examples in this article use API version 2024-10-01. ... $apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com" ... Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put ... "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged: the endpoint is present through variables in the documented PowerShell example. Add to the row note: 'The request body uses scope.environmentId and allocatedEntitlements with entitlementId MCSMessages; allocation.quantity sets credits, and enforcementRules with ruleType TenantPool and enabled sets tenant-capacity draw.'

claims.claim: Environment capacity controls apply across Copilot Studio credit-consuming workloads regardless of harness.
claims.quote: Environment capacity controls apply to all Copilot Studio workloads in the environment, not only agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.claim: The environment group rule Cost controls - Draw from tenant credit pool governs whether environments can use unallocated tenant credits.
claims.quote: Use the Cost controls - Draw from tenant credit pool environment groups rule to control whether environments in a group can use unallocated Copilot Credits from the tenant pool.

claims.claim: Publishing that group rule makes the environment-level setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center, and programmatic requests can't override it.

claims.claim: Programmatic requests cannot override a published environment group rule governing tenant-capacity draw.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.
